Thanks — some concrete numbers below based on current vendor windows and our inventory: 

- H100 reservations: lead time ~4–6 weeks for dedicated cloud reservations (market dependent). Minimum viable for Echelon POC: 6x H100 for first 2 weeks, then scale to 16x H100 for production ramp. If we reserve 16 H100 now (90-day commit) we cover POC + early prod but costs are higher; recommend a staged reservation: 8 H100 reserved (covers POC + partial prod) + 8 H100 on flexible billing.
- A100 reservations: available with ~2–3 week lead. Good for SigmaCloud initial 8xA100 pool.
- Spot/backfill strategy: for lower priority or bursty deals we can rely on spot pools in us-west-2 and us-east-1 with automated fallback.

Risks: vendor supply for H100 could tighten in Aug; if Echelon insists on H100 dedication we should start reservation this week. I can spin a cost delta sheet for the staged option.

Laura/Vivek —

Infra notes & mitigation plan: 
- Current cluster heads in us-west-2 have capacity for an additional ~24 A100-equivalent slots without major re-architecture. H100s require node-level upgrades; provisioning 16 H100s will need a rolling maintenance window (~4 hours) and a kernel push. We can do that on 2026-08-01 or 2026-08-08 (preferred).
- For Echelon POC starting 2026-08-15: to guarantee service-level latency we should reserve the 6 H100s Vivek called out and place an additional 6 H100s as on-demand reserved-capacity—this reduces blast risk if a node fails.
- Short-term burst strategy: split routing by region + model-size. If SigmaCloud needs initial 8 A100, we can place them in us-east-1 (quicker lead) and use cross-region routing for the first 6 weeks.

Action items I can own: schedule maintenance window (ops@infra will coordinate), prepare deployment runbook for node upgrades, and produce a fallback playbook for spot failures. ETA for runbook: EOD Thu 2026-07-16.

-Dylan
